column1: # Realm-tier badge dyn lines (...级...) SKIPPED — they auto-compose
# from 00_morphemes (微尘级=Dust-Tier, 初级=Basic, +=+, etc). Only real descriptions translated.

column2: An ordinary pale-colored slime.
A pale slime that's gained a sword and shield — but it's weighed down in speed.
A mutant slime, overall stronger than an ordinary slime.
A smallish moth; its flight makes it very nimble.
The weakest of undead creatures.
A mutant slime that's gained a sword and shield — this one isn't slowed down anymore!
A young mage. Magic attacks ignore defense, but he's quite fragile himself.
A juvenile beast of the Bloodfall Continent; its meat is fresh and succulent.
A rock puppet nearly out of energy, with only Dust-Tier Advanced strength left.
A mutant slime a size larger, stronger than its kind.
A mutant moth glowing bright, inheriting the Small Moth's agility.
Another advanced mutant slime. Stronger than the black version across the board.
It snatched its sword and shield by its own strength! Don't underestimate it!
A bigger moth, not so agile, but it does a 2-hit combo!
They say everyone who's been through Mind-State 1 has a bit of trauma from it…
Each time you hit it, it loses at most 1 drop of blood~
The embodiment of a nightmare, yet with loot as colorful as a dream!
It's tempered its own bones to a bronze hue — clearly no pushover.
A slightly older mage. Still ignores defense, and much stronger now.
Legend says ordinary/armed slimes shift through rainbow colors as they grow stronger…
Its evolution stage is like the Dust-Tier Ferocious Beast, but its larger size gives it more power… and more meat.
Someone else's kid who snuck into the Na Family to learn techniques — deserves a spanking!
That bud is the crystallization of its cultivation! But an All-Things-Tier one won't sell for a single Copper Coin…
Ave Mujica, "miracles into the everyday" (Fortuna)… not THIS kind of doll!
An ordinary Na Family attendant. Being on a city street, it pulls its punches.
A puppet of painted sheet iron, a bit stronger than its stone brother.
Another member of the Furball family — though only a hair stronger than the Budding Furball.
An Aberrant Beast wielding the power of Restraint. Energized, its meat is highly nutritious.
A puppet of lightweight alloy, trading defense for speed.
A tanky Furball that's learned Magic Attack!
A mass-produced Na Family puppet statue. Not strong, but it's cheap.
Its bud holds ample mana, enough to convert into one Rainbow Gel.
The Red Bat from Floor 24 of the Mage Tower has reincarnated, carrying deepened damage!
Compared to its little brother, an existence forgotten for showing up too late.
A less-desperate Hundred-Clans footsoldier; it leaves once lightly wounded.
A low-rung Bloodfall mercenary, guarding mediocre treasure.
An Aberrant Beast that, thanks to racial advantage, takes a preemptive-strike strategy.
A bizarrely-structured ooze; fight it and your stats get reversed!
A burly youth of Yangang City, among the stronger of his peers.
A mage stronger than the Young Mage, having learned all-new magic.
An undead that's condensed some flesh atop its gathered souls — both offense and defense.
A big rock outside the city. Not very hostile; leaves once lightly wounded.
Furball family — wild limited edition.
A mutant giant wasp. Its venom can enfeeble you.
A butterfly freshly out of its cocoon. Its sharp forelimbs can rend enemies.
A mutant Green Furball. Its irregular shape makes it both nimble and durable.
A common cultivator seen everywhere. Low cultivation, few possessions.
A ghost that survived in the wilds. Very fragile, but erratic and elusive.
A bird-type Wildbeast. Muscular, thick-skinned and tough.
A slightly rarer common cultivator; among the Tide-Tier High-Tier, it counts as strong.
A ground-dwelling Wildbeast; a bit more meat than Wildbeast Nier.
A small Wildbeast famed for speed; it'll snatch a bit of anything.
A puppet spontaneously formed within rock, often with gems embedded inside.
A monster lurking underground, striking precisely where adventurers' defense is weak — extremely tough.
An old man whose potential is spent yet who barely reached Tide-Tier Peak; he'd give anything for a shot at Earth-Tier.
A monster formed from a dead adventurer's grudge. Having died in poverty, it craves money to the last.
The first Earth-Tier enemy. Friendly reminder: XP growth rate doubles from Earth-Tier up!
Don't think about a war of attrition with it… unless you can defense-kill it, of course.
A beefed-up Living-Spirit Skeleton. Its bones are top-grade material!
A Furball holding frenzied power; nearby Wildbeasts are affected by it and turn violent.
The Crypt's only Tide-Tier monster. It survived thanks to the convenience of the light.
Being a branch of a branch of the family, no need to worry the city lord will come after you for hitting him.
A life-form born of pure organized energy. Innately Magic Attack, but very fragile.
Its giant eyeball didn't improve its eyesight… it seems to have forgotten how convex lenses form images.
Its array is a bit slow to set up, but the effect is still strong.
Its absolute darkness reverses the rules of offense and defense. But who says that's necessarily a bad thing?
A demon-puppet that studied Restraint from books in the Crypt. By the way, Restraint has climbed to #2 on the "trap-effect leaderboard"!
He read more books and discovered Restraint is a huge trap. Sadly, its own stats aren't much…
A spiky-ball Furball lurking in the dark. It lost the capture skill — or rather, every monster here has the capture skill.
Ten times stronger when corrupted, a bit weaker when redeemed. Well, you're seeing the former on display~
Its spores carry an enfeebling toxin. Outside, its traces vanished long ago, but in the dark Crypt it spreads everywhere.
Like a true storm! Gale? Merely a clumsy imitation of it!
A noble-blooded Yellow Furball; once it buds, it means entering Earth-Tier. Of course, the 99.8% of Yellow Furballs that drop dead won't have a say.
I was the Wall of Sighs of this place, until Shaxue found an extra 0 in the def…
Now you can't escape… but it's not so strong anymore either!
Its Hurricane mechanic makes it not much easier to handle than the BOSS-tier one…
An elite Wildbeast of the shallow layer; at the core they're so common they've flooded the place.
An evolved ghost of the Crypt. Like all ghost-type monsters, its body is fragile, its attacks fierce.
